articleTitle: Broadband High-Resolution Fourier Spectrometry with Chip-Scale Combs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Electrically-pumped optical frequency combs have emerged as promising candidates for broadband, high-resolution optical sensing. Here we show how their unique emission properties can be leveraged in Fourier spectrometers with millimeter-long optical delays to obtain resolution enhancements by orders of magnitude without any optical setup modifications.

articleTitle: Structured Waveguide Grating for Controlled Resonant Reflection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Waveguide gratings with structured period provide controllable ratio between coupling coefficients in different diffraction orders and allow for control of resonant reflection spectra. We report conceptual model, numerical studies, and fabrication of GaN structured period waveguide gratings designed for the mid-IR spectral range.

articleTitle: Photonic Integrated Circuits in RF Beamforming for Optimized 5G/6G Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We demonstrate new phased array architectures that use photonic integrated circuits (PIC) to process the complete RF beamspace and spectral channelization. Broadband systems based on bulk optical devices will be demonstrated with low noise figure operation (~7 dB) over a 20 to 40 GHz bandwidth as will candidate PIC based implementations.

Author Keywords: beams pace processing and wideband spectral channelization

articleTitle: Topology Optimized Metamaterial Infrared Filters Using Particle Swarm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Development of novel metamaterial-based optical devices typically introduce a primitive unit cell to manipulate the properties of incident radiation. In this work, we employ a novel numerical framework for the design and optimization of exotic unit cells for achieving specified performance metrics.

articleTitle: Concentration of Flurophore Labeled ssDNA Molecules Near Au Nanoparticles by Dielectrophresis Improves the Fluorescence Intensity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We have employed dielectrophoresis to concentrate fluorophore labeled ssDNA molecules in the Au nanoparticles and studied its impact on fluorescence enhancement.

articleTitle: Impact of Fabrication Tolerances on the Performance of Integrated Optics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present a method for predicting the impact of fabrication tolerances of passive components on the performance of photonic integrated circuits (PICs). The outcome is evaluated in a telecommunication modulator evidencing the expected performance impact when a big number of devices is produced..

articleTitle: Ultra-Low Light, Color CMOS Image Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: SIONYX's SXGA, backside illuminated CMOS sensors image below 1 mLux at 90 FPS in a compact, low latency camera. The sensors have NIR QE enhanced using nanotexturing processing, 100% fill factor, read noise of 1.1 e/pix and Bayer filters for color imaging below quarter moon.

articleTitle: Coherent Phonon Decay of Raman Active Vibrations Within Oxide Groups of KTiOPO4
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present on decay of Raman active modes of potassium titanyl phosphate (KTiOPO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) using a tunable ultrafast Coherent Anti-stokes Raman spectroscopy (CARS) system. Decay transients were around 70 dB signal spans with equivalent spectral resolution of better than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.15 \text{cm}^{-1}$</tex> and temporal resolution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 120$</tex> fs.

articleTitle: Metasurfaces Designed on Silicon Nitride Thin Films for Enhanced Mid-Infrared Light Absorption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We report on designs and simulation results of four different metasurfaces that can be patterned out of gold and platinum nanostructures on a 200nm-thick silicon nitride film for band-selective absorption of 3-5μm mid-infrared light. The results demonstrate promising potential for integration with room temperature mid-infrared detectors.

articleTitle: Infrared Metamaterial Spectral Feature Design Utilizing Genetic Algorithm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: This work presents the design testing and evaluation of an infrared absorbing metamaterial. A genetic algorithm was used to optimize spectral features; testing and evaluation has proven that the metamaterial shows good agreement with the designed spectral features across the wavelengths of interest.

Author Keywords: Infrared Metamaterials Genetic Algorithm Design Fabrication

articleTitle: InAs/AlSb Quantum Cascade Detectors Strain-Balanced to GaSb Substrates
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present a study on the growth, design, and characterization of strain-compensated InAs/AlSb quantum cascade detectors (QCDs) on GaSb substrates. A QCD detecting at 4.3 μmwas designed and grown. HR-XRD and AFM confirm high growth quality and successful strain compensation.

articleTitle: Photonic Signal Transport on Aerospace Platforms: is Analog Signaling Ever Useful?
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: For photonic signal transport in multi-GHz, waveform-sensitive RF transport applications, it will be shown that digital-over-fiber fundamentally enables superior SNR performance versus analog-over-fiber. However, for SWaP-constrained systems, the latter can provide a viable solution with minimal SNR penalty.

articleTitle: Frequency Selective Metasurface Fabricated with Two-Photon Polymerization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Metasurfaces, in the form of perfect reflectors, have received attention for their sensing and filtering capabilities. Plas-monic metasurfaces allow for frequency filtering by controlling the input polarization. We demonstrate a frequency filtering metasurface composed of an array of subwavelength metallic pluses fabricated using two-photon polymerization.

articleTitle: microRNA Detection in Heathy and Pancreatic Cancer Samples
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: This study presents a device for accurate microRNA quantification in plasma samples, enhancing early-stage pancreatic cancer diagnosis. Employing dielectrophoretic force and plasmonic based fluorescence enhancement, the device offers precise miRNA quantification, addressing a critical need in cost-effective clinical application.

articleTitle: Dual-Objective Numerical Optimization of MUTC Photodetectors for Frequency Comb Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We calculate phase noise as a function of comb-line frequencies for two modified uni-traveling carrier photodetectors and then optimize the two devices for lower phase noise and higher quantum efficiency using the particle swarm optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: Analysis of Thermal Infrared Detection via Silicon Nitride Trampoline Nanomechanical Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present on a theoretical analysis of ultrasensitive infrared light detection by using silicon nitride (SiN) trampoline nanomechanical resonators. Among the engineering tradeoffs, using a low-stress film may enhance the resonator's response. Optimizing the absorptance with patterned metamaterials is expected to improve the resonance shift by three orders of magnitude.

articleTitle: Dissipative Kerr Soliton for Microcomb Optical Clock: from Dispersion Engineering to Nonlinear Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Frequency combs and an atomic-transition stabilized lasers are the two primary elements of an optical clock. We address the on-chip integration of the comb, including dispersion engineering, photonics' potential for flexible microcombs, and a novel technique for passively synchronizing the master laser and the microcomb.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Optical Properties of Molecular Gold Complexes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Recent advances in the structure, optical spectroscopy, and excited-state dynamics of amine-substituted gold(I) fluorenyls are described. Excited-state kinetic parameters are sensitive to the mode of attachment of gold(I) to fluorenyl (direct attachment, or through alkynyl or triazolyl spacers) and to the ancillary phosphine or carbene ligand on gold. Density-functional theory calculations indicate that the frontier orbitals are dominated by the fluorenyl carbocycle and amine substituent.

articleTitle: Adaptive and Reconfigurable Optical Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Metasurface light manipulation is traditionally achieved through the physical patterning of periodically arranged sub-wavelength unit cells via electron beam lithography. Subsequent etching of these patterned devices has been able to realize surfaces with properties such as near perfect absorption and subwavelength focusing. However, despite these significant achievements, the nano-patterning of most unit cell materials produces static electromagnetic properties that limits the theoretical bounds of performance and functionality. Phase-change materials (PCMs) provide an opportunity to overcome this limitation since they can be transitioned between two material phases with distinct optical properties. Herein, we investigate the use of antimony-trisulfide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{Sb}_{2}\mathrm{S}_{3})$</tex>, a new class of low-loss optical chalcogenide PCMs, for the development of reconfigurable metasurfaces in the infrared (IR). We also investigate vanadium oxide (VOx) metasurfaces for tunable and adaptive controlled thermal IR emissions. The development of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Sb}_{2}\mathrm{S}_{3}$</tex> and VOx based reconfigurable metasurfaces in the IR offer a promising path towards achieving new functionalities and higher overall efficiencies than what are currently achieved today.

articleTitle: MWIR Photodetector Arrays Enhanced by Integration with Si Micropyramidal Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Truncated Si micropyramidal arrays with 60 µm pitch are integrated with 10 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{x}10$</tex> platinum/silicide Schottky barrier photodetectors with 22 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> square mesas. A four times stronger MWIR photoresponse is observed for micropyramidal arrays compared to the conventional planar photodetectors with the same size.

articleTitle: Photonics-Based Real-Time Spectral Analysis Over 40-GHz Bandwidth with Fine Frequency Resolution
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We demonstrate a novel scheme based on electro-optic phase modulation following the Talbot effect that enables real-time spectrogram analysis of arbitrary signals over 40-GHz bandwidth, with MHz frequency resolution, and analysis rates up to 220 million Fourier transforms per second.

articleTitle: Label Free Flow Cytometry Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We have investigated the feasibility of using machine learning analysis for label free and low-cost cell detection for disease detection applications.

articleTitle: Secondary Radiation Generation Using High-Intensity Short-Pulse Lasers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: During propagation in air, high-intensity laser pulses can convert some of their energy into frequencies far from the laser fundamental, simultaneously covering microwaves to the ultraviolet. We present recent progress to understand the mechanisms responsible for low-frequency secondary radiation, and how this may inform designs for next-generation short-pulse lasers.

articleTitle: Harnessing Bound States in the Continuum in Dielectric Gratings for Resonant Mid-Infrared Transmission Filtering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Resonant coupling to bound states in the continuum in periodic sub-wavelength lattices is a means to selectively filter incident radiation. Simulation and experimental results of mid-infrared coupling to one-dimensional and two-dimensional dielectric lattices are described, including spectral, angular incidence, and polarization dependence.

articleTitle: Angular Velocity and Center of Rotation Detection Using Orbital Angular Moment Carrying Beamlets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: This paper introduces a method to measure off axis rotating objects utilizing a structured light sensing scheme. This approach uses a single source to generate frequency tagged Orbital Angular Momentum OAM beamlets that can be used to detect object dynamics using a single detector. Experimental results are provided for an off axis rotating object representational of a propeller-based system.

articleTitle: Experimental Ground Penetrating Radar Imaging via Phase-Encoded Qualitative Inverse Scattering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We experimentally evaluate the phase-encoded linear sampling method (PE-LSM) for ground penetrating radar. The PE-LSM improves upon the conventional LSM for limited aspect arrays by incorporating a propagation-based phase encoding. We demonstrate fundamentally improved fidelity relative to the LSM and improved range resolution compared to backprojection.

articleTitle: Morpho Butterfly-Inspired Device with Functionality in the Near-Infared
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: A Morpho-butterfly-inspired structure was designed to have an optical response in the near infrared and fabricated via multiphoton lithography. The structure produces a peak reflectance of 45% centered at 1529 nm with a full-width at half-maximum of 24.9 nm.

articleTitle: Digital Micromirror Device Enabled Angle of Incidence Control for Microsphere Photolithography
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: A Digital Micromirror Device (DMD) at the Fourier plane provides dynamic angular control at the image plane for microsphere photolithography, allowing for a +/- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$26^{\circ}$</tex> angle to be achieved on a microsphere array. A split ring resonator (SRR) on glass has been fabricated for demonstration.

articleTitle: Towards a Better Scoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel method to calculate trainee performance scores in a flight simulator environment using flight simulator logs. Our approach improves upon the existing scoring system designed in the AFRL by better fitting scores into the existing model of the training process.

articleTitle: Ultrafast Dynamics of Refractory Metals: TiN and ZrN
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Refractory metals such as titanium or zirconium nitride have long been noted for their similarities to noble metals. In ultrafast spectroscopic measurements, however, they show substantially strong electron-phonon coupling, only apparent spectroscopically near intraband transitions, and large lattice heating.

articleTitle: On the Methodology of Modeling a Parallel Plate Capacitor Using the Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: The Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) method is an efficient technique to model the propagation of an electromagnetic field using an equivalent circuit. This work is a methods paper on computing the equivalent PEEC model of a parallel plate capacitor. Results are validated.

articleTitle: Security Challenges for Assurance in Silicon Photonic Packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: As most silicon photonics (SiPH) foundries are located internationally, significant security concerns exist when such devices are outsourced. We investigate critical vulnerabilities in the SiPH supply chain, including Denial of Service (DoS), data leakage, and reliability, and propose physical inspection as a potential security measure.

articleTitle: Effect of Angle of Incidence on Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Structural coloration, which can be controlled by the periodicity of LIPSS on metals is useful for many applications such as counterfeit labeling, and optical encryption. This paper studies the effect of the processing angle of incidence on the periodicity of LIPSS on stainless steel.

articleTitle: Creating Your Own STEM Show with Two Simple Examples
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: In addition to the science you bring, the best outreach shares your personality, so creating your own show is ideal. Everyday items gently draw students in and clearly demonstrate that STEM is all around them. Two conceptually simple science shows are detailed to spark your imagination. A simple machines obstacle course has participants complete the same tasks with and without mechanical advantage. An electricity project has participants make their own series and parallel circuits powered by a recycled adapter that they can take home to run other projects.

articleTitle: A Shot Noise Limited Balanced Microwave Photonic Link Using An LNOI Modulator and An MUTC BPD
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We demonstrate a broadband, positive gain, shot noise limited microwave photonic link using a dual-output lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) modulator and a balanced, high-power photodiode. ~20dB relative intensity noise (RIN) suppression and ~15dB noise figure (NF) at 1GHz are measured for the 20GHz link.

articleTitle: Compressive Spectral-Video by Optimal 3D-Sphere Packing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: This paper introduces a new method to capture compressive spectral video (SV) imaging by exploiting 3-dimensional sphere packing (SP) to design 4D-coded apertures. The proposed approach reconstructs the 4D-hypercube from a single snapshot. Simulations using SV demonstrate the performance of SP approach.

articleTitle: Unilateral Lower Extremity Exoskeleton Utilizing Sensor Fusion Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Electromyography (EMG) and Inertial Measurement (IMU) sensors are increasingly associated with exoskeletons and prosthetics. Coordination and synchronization of these sensors with a sensor fusion algorithm modifying an array of multiple armband sensors allows sensing the user's intended movement and controlling a unilateral lower extremity exoskeleton.

articleTitle: Pound-Drever-Hall Frequency Locking as a Photonic Integrated Circuit Compatible Fibre Bragg Grating Strain Sensing Interrogation Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: The Pound-Drever-Hall frequency locking technique is demonstrated as a photonic integrated circuit compatible interrogation method for optical fibre strain sensing. Static and high frequency signals are measured, and real-time hardware decoupling of static and high frequency acoustic emissions is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Anti-Stokes Photoluminescence from Erbium-Doped Colloidal Lithium Yttrium Fluoride Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Colloidal LiYF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>:Er nanoparticles were synthesized using a co-precipitation approach. Comprehensive structural characterization confirmed their actual composition was very close to the targeted composition, as determined by relative amounts of Y and Er precursors. Observation of anti-Stokes luminescence makes these nanoparticles a candidate for laser cooling applications.

articleTitle: Photonic Reservoir Computing for Spectrum Awareness Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Photonic reservoir computing can perform efficient and ultra-fast information processing in both fiber and radiofrequency (RF) networks. In this communication, we provide an overview of this topic with an emphasis on applications related to RF fingerprinting, cognitive radio, and spectrum awareness.

articleTitle: Using AI-Assisted Inverse Design for Metalens Performance Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: An approach for inverse design of metalenses assisted by artificial intelligence is being developed. The tool will enable metalens design for multi-function applications. The tool will be validated by fabricating devices using multiphoton lithography. A preliminary metalens was fabricated and characterized both structurally and optically.

articleTitle: Hybrid Metasurface with Multipole Resonances for Improved Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We engineer a hybrid plasmonic metasurface with the formation of bound states in the continuum. By controlling multipole Fano resonances and Rabi splitting with individual antenna properties, we experimentally observe Kerker effect in a binary lattice of silicon disks.

articleTitle: Light Manipulation with Si Mesoscale Structures for Applications in IR Photodetector and Photoemitter Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Si anisotropic wet etching is applied to fabricate massive parallel microstructure arrays with novel optical properties. They can be used for enhancing light-concentration properties of mid-IR and long-IR focal plane arrays (FPAs), and for beam-shaping properties of IRLED arrays used in Infrared Scene Projectors (IRSPs).

articleTitle: Development of New Drive Electronics for Infrared Scene Projectors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Infrared Scene Projectors require an efficient set of drive electronics to accurately perform signal manipulation and send the correct image data to be displayed. As these projectors improve, a new generation of drive electronics is required to maintain efficiency and provide signals at greater speeds.

articleTitle: AlGaN Based Emitters and Detectors for Non-Line-of-Sight Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: NLOS communication in the UV is promising for various reasons including improved signal penetration and resistance to interference. Here, progress towards the development of high power UVC LEDs emitting at 265 nm and APDs with sensitivity at the same wavelength for NLOS applications is discussed.

articleTitle: Mid-Infrared Multipole Resonances in Dielectric Metasurfaces with Ultra-High Refractive Indices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We study directional scattering (Kerker effect) in a super-Mossian dielectric <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{FeS}_{2}$</tex>. Its refractive index exceeds the traditional Moss rule by 40%. By exciting multipole lattice resonances near the first-diffraction-order Rayleigh anomaly, we observe behavior similar to electric and magnetic dipoles with Kerker condition fulfilled.

articleTitle: Measuring Refractive Index of Fingerprints
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Advanced biometric applications require estimation of the optical properties of human skin which are often unknown and expensive to obtain. We introduce a simple and fast method to measure the complex index of refraction of human skin and apply it to fingerprints.

articleTitle: Discrepancy-Based Genetic Algorithm Optimization of Quasi-Random Nanostructures for Broadband Light Reflection Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Periodic nanostructures have previously been used to increase the absorption of various semiconductors, but they mainly provide improvement in a specific spectrum. On the other hand, random nanostructures can increase the adsorption over a broad range of frequencies without a targeted frequency. Instead, quasi-random nanostructures have shown broad spectrum improvements and targeted spectrum enhancement compared to both periodic and random nanostructures. Considering an infinite number of quasi-random nanostructures, it is challenging to design or optimize a quasi-random structure pattern via traditional simulations (i.e., Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD), Finite Element Analysis, Rigorous coupled-wave analysis). Discrepancy is a method of measuring surface randomness of a structure. Previous work has shown that a higher star discrepancy, and there for a higher surface randomness, of a quasi-random structure reduces surface reflection and increases optical path length, resulting in a higher absorption for semiconductors. Therefore, discrepancy calculations allow a quasi-random nanostructure to be evaluated more efficiently than running a FDTD simulation. In this paper, we used a genetic algorithm (GA) to optimize the discrepancy of quasi-random nanostructures instead of running thousands of optical simulations for the optimization. The optimized quasi-random sequence is compared with a classical quasi-random Fibonacci sequence. The star discrepancy, or the maximum absolute discrepancy was measured and found to be 0.0026 for a Fibonacci sequence and 0.0387 for the GA generated sequence, an order of magnitude enhancement. The FDTD simulations show that the GA-based quasi-random nanostructure shows a 20% absorption improvement over the Fibonacci sequence at 450 nm wavelength and additionally shows a doubling of absorption in the near-infrared region, suggesting a better antireflection performance.

articleTitle: Leaky-Wave Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We show that symmetry-breaking design principles enable metasurfaces fed from guided modes that radiate with pointwise specification of amplitude, phase, and polarization. We demonstrate this platform for both optical frequency and radiofrequency devices, including beam-steering, polarization-switchable operation, and multiple-input multiple-output functionality.

articleTitle: Multiple UAS/Multiple Sensors for Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaisance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: A system of drones and sensors is designed to obtain situational awareness over large areas for agricultural, environmental assessment, security, and military applications. Sensor roles are divided into wide area coverage and interrogation. The status, modeling, and field results for this system are discussed.

articleTitle: Second Harmonic Generation Enhancement from Isolated Selenium Nanowire Coupled to Mie Resonant Silicon Disks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Optical coupling between heterogenous nanophotonic structures is a promising approach to enhance nonlinear optical response. Here we demonstrate second harmonic generation enhancement by 152-times from an isolated Selenium nanowire coupled to a silicon disk supporting Mie Resonances while maintaining the polarization selectivity of the nanowire.

articleTitle: Radar Applications of a Prototype Dual-Band Metamaterial and Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Current dual-band radars consist of 2 different radar antennas with the same back-end electronics and software. There is great interest in AFRL to develop dual-band radars by using the same antenna, operating at two different frequencies, to achieve the desired efficiency as with traditional systems but without the SWaPC constraints. This article discusses radar applications of a dual-band antenna design made possible by integrating metamaterial and metasurface design elements. The metamaterial component of the design investigates the phase change properties of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$VO_{2}$</tex> as a mechanism for switching the equivalent impedance of the proposed antenna. The meta-surface component of the design investigates the size, arrangement and structure of the antenna's unit cells that allow for both dual-band behavior and beam-steering capabilities. This article discusses the application of the proposed dual-band antenna for detection of and tracking of radar targets.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Risley Prism
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Compared to conventional gimbal systems, Risley Prism beamsteerers are more compact, more resistant to vibration, offer higher scan speeds, and require lower power for operation. By integrating metamaterials, we demonstrate further improvements for future Risey Prism systems by reducing mass and improving scalability.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm Optimizer for Volumetric Metasurface Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: A meta optics design tool is implemented and shown to automatically optimize the topology of three-dimensional meta-atoms to be used in optical applications. The tool can optimize for bandwidth, fabrication limitations, field of view, and device height simultaneously for fully three-dimensional meta-atoms with realistic features.

articleTitle: Dielectric Function of VO2 determined by Spectroscopic Ellipsometry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: The transition metal oxide VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> exhibits a metal-insulator transition and is of interest for dynamic metamaterial applications. Here the complex dielectric function of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, de-posited via magnetron sputtering, is determined below and above the metal-insulator transition temperature using spectroscopic ellipsometry over a wide soectral range.

articleTitle: Mechanical Tuning of Diffractive Gratings Compatible with Two-Photon Polymerization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Recent advances in additive manufacturing have enabled the fabrication of diffractive elements with tailored mechanical properties. This enables the design and fabrication of diffractive optical elements which can be tuned by applying mechanical strain. Here diffractive transmission gratings composed of slanted wires are investigated.

articleTitle: Adaptive Training System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an adaptive training algorithm that accelerates the training process based on a parametric model of trainees and training scenarios. The proposed approach makes trial-by-trial recommendations on optimal scenario difficulty selections to maximize improvements in the trainee's absolute skill level.

articleTitle: Optical Properties of 2D Nonlinear Functional Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: A rigorous first-principles solution of the may-body Semiconductor Dirac Bloch equations describing Transitional Metal Dichalcogenides is incorporated into a software tool to extract critical optical properties such as absorption, gain, photoluminescence and radiative carrier lifetimes.

articleTitle: Graphene Based Field Effect Transistor with Chemical Free p-Type Channel Doping
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: This paper reports transport properties for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Al}_2 \mathbf{O}_3$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex> encapsulated graphene bilayer with strain defined sheet carrier density and mobility of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.65\cdot 10^{13} \text{cm}^{-2}$</tex> and 1275 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{cm}^{2}\mathrm{V}^{-1}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Al}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.96 \cdot 10^{13} \text{cm}^{-2}$</tex> and 795 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{cm}^2 \text{~V}^{-1} \mathbf{s}^{-1}$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex> respectively that were used for the FET fabrication.

articleTitle: Strain Sensitive THz Stereo-Metamaterial based Polarization Conversion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Flexible and reflective stereo-metamaterial (SMM) was fabricated in a stretchable soft backing layer of polydimethylsiloxane and polyimide substrate. Up to 10% strain was applied to interchange the resonant frequency of Cu-coupled metamaterial rings. A redshift was observed in the frequency range after inducing strain.

articleTitle: Degradation of Thermal Emission from Vertically Aligned Carbon Nanotubes Stimulated by Nanosecond Pulsed Laser
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Vertically aligned carbon nanotubes (VACNTs) have shown promise as blackbody sources for IR scene projection when heated by laser pulses. Although VACNTs are fairly robust, degradation is seen after repetitive laser excitations. The degradation starts as oxidation, eventually leading to catastrophic morphological changes.

articleTitle: Integrated Nano-Plasmonic and Dielectrophoretic Based Label Free DNA Biomarker Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We have studied an integrated localized surface plasmon resonance of Au nanoparticles and dielectrophoretic platform for label free detection of short single-stranded DNA molecules.

articleTitle: Propagation of Structured Light Beams in a Turbulent and Turbid Underwater Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Real-world underwater environments present obstacles to optical systems including turbulence and turbidity. The effects of scattering and underwater turbulence on an optical system are observed simultaneously to optimize the propagation of structured beamlets through these conditions with minimized distortion.

articleTitle: CDS's Infrared LED Scene Projector System as a Platform Product
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: With recent improvements to Chip Design System's (CDS's) Infrared LED Scene Projector (IRSP) System, we are happy to announce our IRSP System as a platform product.

articleTitle: Double-Channel Notch Filters Under Angular Tuning on 2D Resonant Gratings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Dual channels of notch filters can be individually controlled by varying two angles of linear-polarized light, which widely expands the tunable range. For long-wave infrared region, we demonstrated germanium-based 2D resonant grating devices. Physical mechanism is clearly explained by guided-mode resonance and effective medium theory.

articleTitle: Waveform Estimation from Nonlinear Systems Using Machine Learning for Rapid Simulation and Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Simulating nonlinear systems featuring a dynamic DSP module is cumbersome, e.g., fiber transport with digital coherent receivers. Machine Learning is used to quickly and accurately estimate waveforms transported through multi-span fiber links over multiple launch powers and OSNRs. Replacing simulation techniques with ML is considered.

articleTitle: Blast Visualization Using NBOS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: NBOS — Natural Background Oriented Shadowgraph technique has been developed for large scale Blast Visualization for qualitative as well as quantitative understanding of blast phenomenon and measurement of blast parameter. The Blast Visualization technique has been reported.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Enabled Material Identification For Uncooled Multispectral Microbolometers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: This study explores machine learning for microbolometer design, evaluation, and selection. A neural net predicts material mixtures for a single pixel using a simulation that predicts multispectral responses relative to a set of basis functions. The study aims to automate AI/ML design and search.

articleTitle: Ultrastable Microwave System for Quantum-enabled Radar Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We present an ultrastable microwave system devoted to synthesizing photonic microwave signals in the RF, L-, S-, and X-bands. The rack-mounted system shows fractional stability below 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-14</sup>level from 100 ms up to 10 hours of operation on a 10 GHz signal, also allowing synchronization with optical clocks.

articleTitle: High Energy Electro-Optically Q-Switched 2.79 μm Cr:Er:YSGG MOPA
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We report on 2.79μm flashlamp-pumped electro optically Q-switched Cr:Er:Ysgg lasers with the La<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf> Q-switch. The “short”(“long”) cavity oscillators demonstrated up to 300(190)mJ output energy in 15(85)ns pulses at a 3Hz repetition rate. In the 2.9m long MOPA configuration, 300mJ was reached at l00ns pulse duration.

articleTitle: Novel Notched Microresonator Design Through Inverse Design Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: Transverse mode overlap creates undesirable mode interactions in microresonators. We use particle swarm optimization to design an AlGaAs microring resonator to significantly increase the transverse mode separation.

articleTitle: Femtosecond Patterning of Monolayer Hexagonal Boron Nitride
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Research and Applications of Photonics in Defense Conference (RAPID)
abstract: We perform the first single shot femtosecond laser ablation and patterning experiments on monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). The observed intrinsic ablation threshold fluence is nearly 809 mJ/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which is 10× higher than all other two-dimensional materials. This indicates monolayer hBN is optically very robust.
